### C1. Site overview ----

```{r}

# read in data for my towers
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

my_towers <- c("CR-AqC", "SE-Svb", "CN-You", "US-Bi2", "AU-Lit")

tower_data <- read_csv("data/snapshots/fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_20261113T112721.csv") %>%
  filter(site_id %in% my_towers)

```


```{r}
 # Lookup-table for site id and country
country_lookup <- tibble(
  site_id = c("CR-AqC", "SE-Svb", "CN-You", "US-Bi2", "AU-Lit"),
  country = c("Costa Rica", "Sweden", "China", "United States", "Australia")
)

# add the country column
tower_data_country <- tower_data %>%
  left_join(country_lookup, by = "site_id")

# correct order
tower_data_overview <- tower_data_country %>%
  select(
    site_id,
    site_name,
    country,
    igbp,
    location_lat,
    location_long,
    first_year,
    last_year,
    data_hub,
    product_citation
  )

# and display table
print(tower_data_overview)

```


```{r}
# create map with site locataioins
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(maps)


# load world map
world_map <- map_data("world")


ggplot() +
  # first the map in the background
  geom_polygon(
    data = world_map,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "lightgray",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # add the location points
  geom_point(
    data = tower_data_overview,
    aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat, color = site_id),
    size = 4,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  # add site name tags
  geom_text(
    data = tower_data_overview,
    aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat, label = site_id),
    vjust = -1,
    size = 3.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # axes
  labs(
    title = "Locations of my FLUXNET-towers",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    color = "Site ID"
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

```

### C2. Data coverage -----


```{r}
# create object hh_all that contains the data of all the towers (from exercise B)
### B3 Wrap it in a function -----------------------------------------
read_hh <- function(zip_file) {
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)

  # define the columns that we want to use
  keep <- c("TIMESTAMP_START", "TIMESTAMP_END", "TA_F", "SW_IN_F", "VPD_F", "P_F",
            "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS_QC", "LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS_QC",
            "NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE_VUT_REF_QC", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF")

  # ZIP-Dateinamen extrahieren (z. B. "prefix_US-Bi2.zip")
  file_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(zip_file))
  site_name <- strsplit(file_name, "_")[[1]][2]  # Zweiter Teil nach dem ersten "_"

  hh_name <- grep("FLUXMET_HH", unzip(zip_file, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)

  unzip(zip_file, files = hh_name, exdir = "data/raw/unzipped")

  # read in csv
  hh_all <- read_csv(file.path("data/raw/unzipped", hh_name),
                     na = "-9999",
                     col_select = any_of(keep),
                     col_types = cols(TIMESTAMP_START = "c", TIMESTAMP_END = "c", .default = "d")) |>
    mutate(time = as.POSIXct(TIMESTAMP_START, format = "%Y%m%d%H%M", tz = "UTC")) %>%
    mutate(site = site_name)  # site-Kürzel basierend auf dem ZIP-Dateinamen hinzufügen

  return(hh_all)
}

	# Get all zip archives
	zip_files <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
	# Apply `read_hh` to each archive and combine the results
	hh_all <- lapply(zip_files, read_hh) |> bind_rows()

```


```{r}
# 
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)  # to get the year out of Postix
library(tidyr)      # to change in not long format for the heat map

# prepare data for visualisation
hh_coverage <- hh_all %>%
  # get the year
  mutate(year = year(time)) %>%
  # calculate proportion of NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0 per site and year
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  summarise(
    share_measured = mean(NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # fill up missing site+ year info with 0
  complete(site, year, fill = list(share_measured = 0))

# change format into not-long-format for the heat map
hh_coverage_wide <- hh_coverage %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = share_measured
  )

```

```{r}
### Print the heat map
ggplot(hh_coverage, aes(x = year, y = site, fill = share_measured)) +
  # Heatmap-Zellen
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  # Farbskala (von 0 bis 1)
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "darkgreen",
    name = "proportion of measured NEE"
  ) +
  # Achsenbeschriftungen
  labs(
    title = "share of half hours in which NEE was measured",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Site"
  ) +
  # Design anpassen
  theme_minimal() +

    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),

  )
```

### C3. Summary statistics ------



```{r}
# data subset site for US
filtered_US <- hh_all[hh_all$site == "US-Bi2", ]

# Function to calculate statistics
calculate_stats <- function(data, variable) {
 
  mean_val <- mean(data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE)
  min_val <- min(data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE)
  missing_pct <- mean(is.na(data[[variable]])) * 100

  data.frame(
    Variable = variable,
    Mean = mean_val,
    Minimum = min_val,
    Maximum = max_val,
    `Missing values (%)` = missing_pct
  )
}

# vector with columns to calculate statistics
variables <- c("TA_F", "SW_IN_F", "VPD_F", "P_F", "NEE_VUT_REF", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF", "H_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS")

# catlucate statistics and store in a list
stats_list_US <- lapply(variables, function(var) calculate_stats(filtered_US, var))

# create one data frame
stats_df_US <- do.call(rbind, stats_list_US)

# transpone table
stats_df_transposed_US <- t(stats_df_US[, -1])  # delete 'variables'
stats_df_transposed_US <- as.data.frame(stats_df_transposed_US)
colnames(stats_df_transposed_US) <- stats_df_US$Variable  
rownames(stats_df_transposed_US) <- c("Mean", "Minimum", "Maximum", "Missing values (%)") 


new_colnames <- c(
  "Air temperature(°C)",
  "solar radiation (W/m²)",
  "VPD (kPa)",
  "Precipiatation (mm)",
  "NEE (µmol CO₂/m²/s)",
  "GPP (µmol CO₂/m²/s)",
  "RECO (µmol CO₂/m²/s)",
  "Sensible heat flux (W/m²)",
  "Latent heat flux  (W/m²)"
)

colnames(stats_df_transposed_US) <- new_colnames

```

### C5. Diurnal cycles -----

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

flux <- hh_all
meta <- tower_data


```

```{r}
# apparently there are still -9999 values uinstead of NAs in the object. I don#t know how, they shouldn#t be there as they were redefined when the data was read in. But somehow I still need to do this but only for Sweden.
flux$NEE_VUT_REF[flux$NEE_VUT_REF == -9999] <- NA
flux$LE_F_MDS[flux$LE_F_MDS == -9999] <- NA
```


```{r}
flux <- flux %>%
  left_join(meta %>% select(site_id, location_lat), by = c("site" = "site_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    month = month(time),
    # define months for season
    season_north = case_when(
      month %in% c(12, 1, 2)  ~ "Winter",
      month %in% c(3, 4, 5)   ~ "Spring",
      month %in% c(6, 7, 8)   ~ "Summer",
      month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Autumn"
    ),
    # Southern hemisphere (lat < 0): season changed by six months
    season = case_when(
      location_lat >= 0 ~ season_north,
      season_north == "Winter" ~ "Summer",
      season_north == "Summer" ~ "Winter",
      season_north == "Spring" ~ "Autumn",
      season_north == "Autumn" ~ "Spring"
    ),
    season = factor(season, levels = c("Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter"))
  )
```

The seasons are defined by month, not by a calender date. The latitude data is attached to define whether site are located on the northern or southern hemisphere. If situated on the southern hemisphere, seasons are reversed. 

```{r}
# calculate mean diurnal fluc
diurnal <- flux %>%
  mutate(hour = hour(time) + minute(time) / 60) %>%   # half-hours
  group_by(site, season, hour) %>%
  summarise(
    NEE = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE),
    LE  = mean(LE_F_MDS,  na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(NEE, LE), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value")
```


```{r}
ggplot(diurnal, aes(x = hour, y = value, color = site)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ season, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Hour of day",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Site",
    title = "Mean diurnal cycle of NEE and LE by season",
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### C6. Energy balance


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


flux <- flux %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ na_if(., -9999)))

# find tower with netrad and g
flux %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(
    n_netrad = sum(!is.na(NETRAD)),
    n_G      = sum(!is.na(G_F_MDS)),
    n_both   = sum(!is.na(NETRAD) & !is.na(G_F_MDS))
  )
```



```{r}
site_sel <- "SE-Svb"   # Sweden

eb <- flux %>%
  filter(site == site_sel,
         H_F_MDS_QC  == 0,
         LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) %>%
  mutate(
    turb  = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS,   # turbulent fluxes (y-axis)
    avail = NETRAD - G_F_MDS      # available energy (x-axis)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(turb), !is.na(avail))
```


```{r}
# fit a linear regression
fit <- lm(turb ~ avail, data = eb)

slope     <- coef(fit)[["avail"]]
intercept <- coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]]
r2        <- summary(fit)$r.squared

slope; intercept; r2
```

```{r}
# Plotting
lims <- range(c(eb$avail, eb$turb), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(eb, aes(x = avail, y = turb)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red", linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text",
           x = lims[1], y = lims[2], hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
           label = sprintf("Slope = %.2f\nR² = %.2f", slope, r2)) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = lims, ylim = lims) +
  labs(
    x = expression(R[n] - G~"(W m"^-2*")"),
    y = expression(H + LE~"(W m"^-2*")"),
    title = paste("Energy balance closure:", site_sel)
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
```

Generally the ecosystem in Costa Rica seems to take up the most carbon when we look at the whole year. The carbon and laten heat fluxes also are the most constant at this tower, which is not surprising as it is a tropical forest there. However, midday carbon fixation rates are very high ( higher than Costa Rica) at the cropland in the United States. This is also the site taht shows the highest variabilty through the seasons. This, however, is also not surprising as crops grow fast but then get harvested. Surprising was the high latent heat flux in the Australian savannah in Autumn. The data from the swedish tower data was annoying to handle as the exchange of the -9999 with the NAs didn't work and I couldn't find the problem for a long time. The data covoreage however, is not too good, especially for the tower in Costa Rica. this tower doensn't have data anymore for the last ten years.
